ARTICLE XI
WORKING CONDITIONS

A. Union Shop Cards may be displayed in markers which employ members of the Union. The Local Union Secretary-Treasurer or his authorized agent has the full power to remove said card upon violation of any part of this Contract. Cards will be displayed in a conspicuous place.

B. Business Agents of the Union shall be admitted at all reasonable times to the working room or rooms and interview the employees covered by this Agreement.

C. As the employees engaged under this Agreement can be members of the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union, nothing in this Contract shall be construed as to interfere with any lawful obligation which they may be subject to as members of Food and Commercial Workers International Union as members thereof.

D. The Union agrees to cooperate in correcting inefficient employments of employees which might otherwise necessitate discharge.

E. The employer agrees not to enter into any agreement or understanding with any employee covered by this Contract, individually or collectively, which would limit the benefits of this Agreement.

F. The Employer shall furnish all necessary tools of the trade, laundry, hairnet and/or uniforms when required, provide the Employer, whenever applicable, shall furnish to the female employees adornment uniforms or similar type uniforms. The employees who are furnished such uniforms shall be responsible in the event for the loss of these uniforms and such uniforms shall be laundered by the employees.

G. The Employer will provide bulletin boards or equivalent notice place in a section suitable selected by the Union. The Employer may post notices necessary for conducting Union business on such boards or other suitable space.

H. Contributions to charitable causes shall not be compulsory.

I. The Employer agrees to furnish and maintain a first aid kit in a designated place and to check said kit monthly to replenish any designated supplied pieces.

J. Employee agree to provide guards on grinders and cube machines. No employee shall use a grinder without the guard on the mill or use the cube machine with the lid or guard up. Any employee using the above equipment without the safety guards shall be subject to discipline, including discharge, without recourse to the arbitration.

K. No employee will be required to report for work until said employee has had a minimum of (10) ten hours off duty.

L. Employees shall not be required to take a polygraph test.

ARTICLE XII
GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION

A. The Employer recognizes the right of the Union to designate one (1) Shop Steward in each market. Such steward shall be designated in writing to the Employer by the Union.

B. Should any differences, disputes, or complaints arise over the interpretation or application of the contents of this Contract, there shall be an efficient sort of the amounts of the party both seres to promptly settle through the following procedure:

Step 1. By conference between the aggrieved employee, the Shop Steward, or Business Agent, and the Manager, and the store of the Manager.

Step 2. By a conference between the Shop Steward or the Business Agent of the Union and the Zone Manager, District Manager or District Supervisor of the Employer, if such exists, within five (5) working days after the completion of Step 1.

Step 3. By a conference between an official of the Union and a designated official of the Employer, within five (5) working days after the completion of Step 2.

Step 4. In the event the grievance is not settled through the abovementioned steps, it shall be referred to arbitration.

C. Grievances must be reduced to writing by the aggrieved employee after the completion of Step 2 in order to be considered under Step 3 and prior to be submitted in writing to official in lieu of notices.

D. Grievances presented later than seven (7) calendar days after the occurrence of the event complained of will not be considered.

E. The grievance that issues may arise of a general nature affecting nature or extending to more than one (1) employee covered by this Contract and that issues need not be subject to the entire grievance procedure, but may be initiated at any of the above-mentioned steps deemed appropriate by the Union representative handling the grievance.

F. It is understood that the Union Grievance Committee shall make the final decision as to arriving at a settlement or any grievance initiated by an employee covered by this Contract. No grievance shall be submitted to arbitration without the approval of the Union representative of the Union Grievance Committee.

G. It is understood and agreed and all employees covered by this Contract must exercise all their rights, privileges, and necessary procedures under this Contract in the settlement of any complaint or grievance.

H. One (1) person shall be appointed by the Employer and one (1) person shall be appointed by the Union (if two (2) persons are unable to settle the complaint, either the Employer or the Union may, within the two (2) days since the complaint, disagree the Request of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service to appoint an impartial arbitrator. The third person shall be the Arbitrator shall be chosen. The decision of the Arbitrator shall be binding on all parties. The Union shall strike a name from the pen, then the Employer shall strike a name, in this order, until one (1) person's name remains, who shall be the Arbitrator. The expenses of the representative of the Arbitrator shall be paid for equally by the Employer and the Union.

I. The Employer may, at any time, at discharge, any worker for just cause. The Union, if it wishes to contest the discharge, may file a written complaint with the Employer within five (5) working days. Such complaint must be taken up promptly and shall be settled within five (5) working days or within forty-eight (48) hours, it shall be referred, within twenty-four (24) hours, to arbitration.

J. No Arbitrator shall have the authority to alter, amend or change any term or provisions of this Contract.

ARTICLE XIII
SEPARATION PAY

A full-time employee will receive no more than six (6) months' full-time service, who is permanently reduced separation the functions of the job, store closing or reduction in the working forces, shall be given one (1) week's notice or one (1) week's pay in lieu of notice. An employee separated during a week for any of these reasons is entitled to pay their pension up to the day of his dismissal, plus one day for an additional week notice, which, at the option of the Employer, may be paid in week or in lieu of notice.

ARTICLE XIV
HEALTH AND WELFARE

A. The Employer shall contribute to the established Health and Welfare Trust Fund the sum of one hundred ninety-one dollars and eleven cents quarterly ($191.11) per month for each employee who has completed an average of twenty-four (24) hours per week for a period of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours) and shall continue to contribute one hundred ninety-one dollars and eleven cents quarterly ($191.11) per month for each employee who maintains an average of twenty-four (24) hours per week for a period of four (4) consecutive calendar weeks (96 hours). Employees who are off work and receiving Employer sickness pay and/or accident benefits shall have such time counted as hours worked immediately preceding the first day of the calendar month.
